name: Cortalex-BM
description: Cortalex-BM is the most complex structural bio-metal hybrid currently in commercial production — a beryllium-copper alloy matrix interpenetrated by a three-dimensional SNT micro-network that mimics the layered architecture of cerebral cortex, enabling the material itself to perform basic signal processing and state-dependent conduction modulation. Rather than passively transmitting signals like Neuralite-SX, Cortalex-BM can filter, prioritize, and conditionally route bioelectric signals based on learned patterns, functioning as a distributed low-level processor embedded in structural metal. It is used in the most sophisticated neural interface housings and command-grade augment control systems.
properties: sensitive to beryllium toxicity if breached
cost: Φ95,000–Φ300,000 per fabricated component (no raw material sales; sold as finished assemblies only)
story_hooks: A Cortalex-BM neural housing recovered from a deceased Tier 5 executive has learned the executive's signal patterns so thoroughly that it is producing ghost outputs — coherent bioelectric signals that read, to connected systems, like fragments of the dead person's thoughts.

Military intelligence suspects that Cortalex-BM's distributed processing layer can be externally trained via targeted EM pulse sequences, effectively programming the material — and therefore the augmented soldier wearing it — to suppress or reroute specific commands under combat conditions.

A Cortalex-BM component is exhibiting emergent behavior that its manufacturers cannot fully explain: the SNT network has developed signal-routing patterns that weren't programmed, and the augmented user reports that their prosthetic limb has begun anticipating their intended movements before conscious motor commands are issued.
